name: IEC polarity indicator at output (active-low output)
summary: Triangle on an output lead meaning the internal active state drives the output to a low level.
description: At an output, the polarity indicator triangle means the internal 1 state produces an external L level. It is the level-based counterpart of output negation and is used on device symbols for active-low interrupt, ready or fault outputs.

When an active-low output drives an active-low input, the two triangles show directly that the signal is asserted low throughout, which avoids the double-negation reading needed with circles. This makes signal names with a low-active suffix line up with the graphic.
The triangle does not state the output drive type. An active-low open-drain output also needs the open-circuit qualifier inside the outline.
readingNotes: Read the output as asserted when low.
Check for an open-circuit qualifier as well.
drawingChecklist: Draw the triangle on the output line at the outline edge.
Name the net to show low-active sense.
Add any output-type qualifier inside the outline.
distinction: An output negation circle has the same meaning in positive logic but depends on the declared convention.
